title: Permutation of a symmetric function's Fourier component
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose constant-one vector is indexed by a distinguished element of a finite nonempty index set. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ invariant under every permutation of its $n$ coordinates, every permutation $\sigma$ of those coordinates, and every subset $S$ of the coordinate set, permuting the input of the Fourier component of $f$ whose indices are nonconstant exactly on $S$ yields the Fourier component whose indices are nonconstant exactly on $\sigma(S)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a basis of real-valued functions, orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by a distinguished element of a finite nonempty index set
$f$ is invariant under every permutation of its $n$ coordinates
$\sigma$ is a permutation of the coordinate set
$S$ is a finite subset of the coordinate set
